Rashi on Ketubot 19a:10:1.hebrew: שחב לאחרים - בהודאה זו שהוא מודה שהוא שטר אמנה, חב ומפסיד את אחרים הנושים בו, ואין לו מה להגבותם, והיו רוצים לגבות חוב זה:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:10:1.english: Where he causes loss to others - By this admission, in which he admits that it is a note of trust, he causes loss and detriment to others who are his creditors, and he has nothing from which to let them collect, and they wanted to collect this debt.

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:11:1.hebrew: ונתן לאשר אשם לו - ולא כתב לאשר הלוהו, אלא לאשר האשם שלו, ואשם הוא קרן, כדאמרי' בהגוזל (ב"ק דף קי.), למי שהקרן שלו:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:11:1.english: And he shall give to the one to whom he is guilty [asham] - [Scripture] did not write "to the one who lent to him," rather "to the one to whom the asham belongs," and asham is the principal, as we say in [the chapter] HaGozel (Bava Kamma 110a): "to the one to whom the principal belongs."

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:1:1.hebrew: אא"כ נעשה בגדול - כל מעשה השטר בגדולים, הלוקח והמוכר. וגבי עדים נמי אמרי', חזקה אין הלוקח מחתים בו קטנים:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:1:1.english: Unless it was made by an adult - [That is,] the entire execution of the document [was] with adults — the buyer and the seller. And regarding witnesses as well, we say [there is] a presumption [that] the buyer does not have minors sign on it.

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:1:2.hebrew: אלא אנוסים מ"ט לא - נימא הפה שאסר הוא שהתיר:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:1:2.english: However, [if they say they were] compelled, why not - [why should we not] say, "the mouth that prohibited is the mouth that permitted"?

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:2:1.hebrew: יהרגו ואל יחתמו שקר - הלכך, כי אמרי נמי אנוסים היינו מחמת נפשות, משוו נפשייהו רשעים:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:2:1.english: They should be killed and not sign a falsehood - Therefore, even when they say, "We were coerced due to [danger to our] lives," they render themselves wicked.

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:4:1.english: One who admits regarding a document that he wrote it - A borrower who admitted regarding a document that he wrote it, and at his instruction the witnesses signed [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:4:2.hebrew: אין המלוה צריך לקיימו - בעדים החתומים בו, שאין הלוה שוב נאמן לומר "פרעתיו", ולא אמרינן בהאי "הפה שאסר הוא שהתיר", דמכיון שאמר כשר היה — הרי הוחזק השטר, וכי אמר "פרעתיו" לא מהימן, שהרי ביד המלוה הוא. ור"מ נמי, דאמר אין נאמנים לפוסלו, במודה לוה שכתבו קאמר, וקסבר לא צריכינן תו לעדים, ולאו אפומייהו מיקיים שטרא:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:4:2.english: The lender need not ratify it - through the witnesses signed on it, for the borrower is no longer believed to say, "I have repaid it," and we do not say in this [case], "the mouth that prohibited is the mouth that permitted," because once he said it was valid, the document is established [as authentic], and when he says, "I have repaid it," he is not believed, since it is in the lender's possession. And Rabbi Meir as well, who says [the witnesses] are not believed to invalidate it, is speaking of [a case] where the borrower admits that he wrote it, and he holds [that] we no longer need the witnesses, and the document is not ratified by their word.

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:5:1.hebrew: גנבא - מתגנב אתה לומר דבריך בלשון שלא נחלקו בו היחיד והמרובים, כדי שלא יבטלו את דבריך, דאמרת כיחידאה:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:5:1.english: Thief - You are acting stealthily to state your words in a manner over which the individual [Sage] and the majority did not dispute, so that they will not invalidate your words [on the grounds] that you spoke like an individual [opinion].

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:5:2.hebrew: אי סבירא לך כר"מ, אימא הלכה כר"מ - ולא תנקוט לה כמילתא באנפי נפשה:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:5:2.english: If you hold like Rabbi Meir, say: The halakha is like Rabbi Meir - And do not state it as a matter unto itself.

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:6:1.english: And what does the Master hold - Regarding one who admits to a document that he wrote [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:6:2.english: When they come before us - Creditors bringing documents.

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:6:3.hebrew: קיימו שטרייכו - כך אני רגיל לומר למלוים המביאים שטרותיהם לפני ואין עדיהם עמהם. אני אומר להם: לכו ובקשו עדיכם וקיימוהו, דאי לאו הכי, אע"ג דמודה לוה שכתבו, מצי למימר פרעתיו:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:6:3.english: Ratify your documents - This is what I am accustomed to say to lenders who bring their documents before me when their witnesses are not with them. I say to them: Go and seek your witnesses and ratify it, for otherwise, even though the borrower admits that he wrote it, he can say, "I paid it."

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:7:1.hebrew: שטר אמנה - לא לוה כלום, אלא כתבו ומסרו למלוה, שאם יצטרך ללות ילוה, והאמינו שלא יתבענו אא"כ מלוהו:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:7:1.english: A document of trust - He did not borrow anything; rather, he wrote it and handed it over to the lender, so that if he needs to borrow, he will borrow [with it], and he trusted him that he would not demand [payment] from him unless he lends [the money] to him.

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:8:1.hebrew: כל כמיניה - והלא עדים חתומים בו? פשיטא דיתקיים בחותמיו:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:8:1.english: Is it within his power - Are there not witnesses signed on it? [It is] obvious that it is ratified by its signatories.

Rashi on Ketubot 19a:9:1.hebrew: כדרב הונא - ואשמעינן רב יהודה נמי הכי, דלוה שאמר: "כתבתיו ומסרתיו לו, אבל שטר אמנה הוא", אין צריך המלוה לחזור ולהביא עדים להעיד על החתימה, דאין נאמן לוה לפוסלו, דלא עביד איניש דכתב ומסר בלא הלואה:
Rashi on Ketubot 19a:9:1.english: In accordance with [the statement of] Rav Huna - And Rav Yehuda teaches us this as well: that [in the case of] a borrower who said, "I wrote it and handed it over to him, but it is a document of trust," the lender does not need to go back and bring [witnesses] to testify about the signature, for a borrower is not believed to disqualify it, since a person does not write [a document] and hand [it] over without a loan.

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:10:1.hebrew: וכגון שחב לאחרים - וא"ת ולהימניה במגו דאי בעי מחיל ליה, דהא המוכר שטר חוב לחבירו וחזר ומחלו מחול (לקמן כתובות דף פה:)? ויש לומר דלאו מגו הוא, דשמא אין דעתו למחול ולהפסיד חובו, דעכשיו שאומר אמנה הוא לא מפסיד מידי, כיון שאין הלוה גזלן. אע"ג דבספ"ק דב"מ (דף כ: ושם) אמרינן מגו כה"ג גבי מצא שובר בזמן שהאשה מודה יחזיר לבעל, דקאמר ש"מ איתא לדשמואל; שמא התם סמכינן אמגו כל דהו משום דאיכא שובר דמוכח. ואם נאמר דמכירת שטר חוב אינו אלא מדרבנן, הוה אתי שפיר, דמצינן למימר: דווקא מוכר שטר חוב, דהוי מדרבנן, יכול למחול, אבל בנושה בחבירו כו', דחייב לו מן התורה, אינו יכול למחול. וכן משמע בפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קמז: ושם) דקאמר: "ומודה שמואל דאם נתנו במתנת ש"מ שאינו יכול למחול", ומסיק: "מתנת ש"מ דאורייתא ואינו יכול למחול, דאי ס"ד מדרבנן, אמאי אינו יכול למחול?" — משמע דבמידי דאורייתא אינו יכול למחול. ויש לדחות, דהתם ודאי אי מתנת שכיב מרע דאורייתא אין היורש יכול למחול, דמאי אולמיה האי יורש מהאי יורש. ועוד יש להביא ראיה דנושה בחבירו וחבירו בחבירו אינו יכול למחול, דאמרי' בסוף האשה שנפלו (לקמן כתובות פא:): "הרי שהיה נושה באחיו מנה ומת והניח שומרת יבם, לא יאמר: הואיל ואני יורש החזקתי, אלא מוציאין מידו ולוקח בהן קרקעות והוא אוכל פירות", ומוקמי' לה כר' נתן; דהא הוי כמו נושה בחבירו מנה וחבירו בחבירו, דכל אשר לבעלה משועבד לה לכתובתה, ואי יכול למחול, אמאי ילקח בהן קרקע? ימחול לעצמו, שהוא יורש ויכול למחול! ויש לדחות, דשאני התם דאין יורש אלא מכחה, ואינו יכול להפקיע זכותה. [וי"מ דדוקא במוכר שט"ח יכול למחול, שקדם חובו של מוכר, אבל הנושה בחבירו, שקדם חובו לחוב של חבירו, אינו יכול למחול; ושומרת יבם נמי, קדם שטר חובה לחוב בעלה.] וא"ת: אכתי נהימניה במגו דאי בעי קלתיה, כדאמרינן בסוף זה בורר (סנהדרין דף לא:)? ויש לומר דהכא אתחזק בבי דינא, דאמרינן התם: כיון דאתחזק בבי דינא, אי בעי קלתיה לא אמרינן; אי נמי, הכא מיירי כשהשטר הוא ביד שליש:
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:10:1.english: And where he causes loss to others - And if you ask: Let us believe him [that it is a document of trust] through a migu [that is, since] if he wanted he could have waived it [the debt], for one who sells a promissory note to another and then waives it, it is waived (below, Ketubot 85b)? And one can say that it is not a [valid] migu, for perhaps he has no intention to waive [it] and lose his debt; whereas now, when he says it is [a document of] trust, he loses nothing, since the borrower is not a robber. Even though at the end of the first chapter of Bava Metzia (20b, and there [in the parallel discussions]) we say such a migu regarding [the case of] one who finds a receipt [for a ketubah, where the Mishnah states:] "When the wife admits [it], he shall return [it] to the husband," where [the Gemara] says: "Conclude from this that [the law] accords with Shmuel" — perhaps there we rely on a weak migu because there is a receipt that proves [the claim]. And if we say that the sale of a promissory note is only rabbinic, it works out well, for we can say: specifically one who sells a promissory note, which is rabbinic, can waive [it], whereas in [the case of] one who has a claim against his fellow [and his fellow against another, etc.], where he is obligated to him by Torah law, he cannot waive [it]. And so it is implied in the chapter Mi SheMeit (Bava Batra 147b, and there), where it says: "And Shmuel concedes that if he gave it as a gift of a dying person, he cannot waive [it]," and it concludes: "A gift of a dying person is by Torah law, and [therefore] he cannot waive [it]; for if it entered your mind [that it is] rabbinic, why can he not waive [it]?" — implying that in a matter of Torah law he cannot waive [it]. And one can reject [this proof], for there, certainly, if a gift of a dying person is by Torah law, the heir cannot waive [it], for what is the greater strength of this heir over that heir? And furthermore, one can bring a proof that [when] one has a claim against his fellow and his fellow against another, he cannot waive [it], for we say at the end of [the chapter] HaIshah SheNafalu (below, Ketubot 81b): "If one had a claim of a maneh against his brother, and [the brother] died and left a shomeret yavam [a widow awaiting levirate marriage], he should not say: 'Since I am the heir, I have taken possession [of it]'; rather, we extract [it] from his hand and purchase land with it, and he consumes the produce," and we establish it in accordance with Rabbi Natan; for this is like one who has a claim of a maneh against his fellow and his fellow against another, since everything belonging to her husband is mortgaged to her for her ketubah. And if he could waive [it], why should land be purchased with it? Let him waive [the debt] to himself, since he is the heir and can waive [it]! And one can reject [this proof], for it is different there, since he is only an heir by virtue of her, and he cannot abrogate her right. [And some explain that specifically in the case of one who sells a promissory note can he waive [it], because the seller's debt preceded [the buyer's]; whereas one who has a claim against his fellow, where his [first creditor's] debt preceded his fellow's debt, he cannot waive [it]. And [in the case of] a shomeret yavam as well, her debt document preceded her husband's debt.] And if you ask: Still, let us believe him through a migu [that] if he wanted he could have burned it, as we say at the end of [the chapter] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 31b)? And one can say that here it was already established in court, for we say there: once it has been established in court, we do not say "if he wanted he could have burned it." Alternatively, here we are dealing with [a case] where the document is in the hand of a third party.

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:11:1.hebrew: מנין לנושה בחבירו כו' - משמע דהלכה כר' נתן, ובגיטין (דף לז.) פירשנוה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:11:1.english: "From where [is it derived that] one who has a claim against his fellow, etc." - This implies that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Natan, and in Gittin (37a) we have explained it.

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:1:1.hebrew: חזקה אין כו' - הכא משמע דלא אמרינן מגו במקום חזקה, ולרבנן אמרינן. וצ"ע, דבעיא היא בפרק קמא דב"ב (דף ה: ושם) ולא אפשיטא, גבי תבע אחר זמנו ואמר ליה: "פרעתיך תוך זמני":
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:1:1.english: There is a presumption [that witnesses do] not [sign], etc. - Here it is implied that we do not say migo against a presumption, whereas according to the Rabbis, we do say [it]. And this requires further study, for it is a question in the first chapter of Bava Batra (5b, and there) and it was not resolved, regarding [a case where a lender] claimed [repayment] after its due date, and [the borrower] said to him, "I paid you within my [allotted] time."

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:3:1.hebrew: דאמר מר אין לך דבר כו' - פירוש: אפי' מאן דמחמיר לא מחמיר אלא בהנך; דרבא גופיה קסבר דאפילו בהני אינו חייב למסור עצמו בצינעא, במס' ע"ז בפרק ר' ישמעאל (עבודה זרה דף נד. ושם), ואין חילוק בין הנך לשאר, ובפרהסיא בכולהו יהרג ולא יעבור:
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:3:1.english: "As the Master said: You have no matter, etc." - Explanation: Even one who is stringent is only stringent regarding these [three sins]; for Rava himself holds that even regarding these, one is not obligated to give up his life in private — [as stated] in tractate Avodah Zarah, in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael (Avodah Zarah 54a and there [elsewhere]) — and there is no difference between these and other [sins], whereas in public, for all of them one must be killed rather than transgress.

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:4:1.hebrew: טעמא דר"מ כדרב הונא כו' - פירש בקונטרס דמיירי פלוגתייהו בשמודה לוה שכתבו, והיינו טעמא דר"מ דאין נאמנין, דהואיל ולוה קיימו לא צריכי תו לעדים ולאו אפומייהו מקיים שטרא, ורבנן סברי צריך לקיימו. וקשה לר"י, דא"כ ליפלגו בלא עדים בלוה גופי', הואיל וטעמייהו תלי בלוה. ועוד, דבפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קנד: ושם) משמע דלא פליגי בלוה, דקאמר רבי יוחנן: "שאני אומר מודה בשטר שכתבו א"צ לקיימו דברי הכל היא", ופריך: "והא מפלג פליגי, אין נאמנים לפוסלו כו'", אמר ליה: "אי אלימי עדים לאורועי שטרא, איהו כל כמיניה". ועוד, דהוה ליה למימר: "בדרב הונא קמיפלגי". ונראה לר"ת ולר"י דה"פ: "טעמא דר"מ כדרב הונא" — דכמו שאומר רב הונא דלא אמרינן מגו לפסול השטר בלוה, ה"נ אומר ר"מ בעדים, דאע"ג דאלימי — לא פסלי שטרא במגו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:4:1.english: "The reason for Rabbi Meir's opinion is in accordance with Rav Huna, etc." - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that their dispute refers to a case where the borrower admits that he wrote it, and this is Rabbi Meir's reason that [the witnesses] are not believed: because since the borrower has ratified it, [the lender] no longer needs the witnesses, and it is not on their word that the document is ratified; whereas the Rabbis hold that it must be ratified [by witnesses]. However, this is difficult for the Ri: for if so, let them disagree without witnesses, regarding the borrower himself, since their dispute depends on the borrower! And furthermore, in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 154b, and there [in the parallel]), it is implied that they do not disagree regarding the borrower, as Rabbi Yochanan says: "For I say that [the principle] 'one who admits with regard to a document that he wrote it need not ratify it' is the view of all," and [the Gemara] objects: "But do they not disagree: 'They are not believed to invalidate it, etc.'?" [And] he said to him: "If witnesses have the power to undermine a document, does he [the borrower] have the power [to do so]?" And furthermore, [the Gemara] should have said: "They disagree regarding [the statement of] Rav Huna." Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam and to the Ri that this is its explanation: "The reason for Rabbi Meir's opinion is in accordance with Rav Huna" — just as Rav Huna says that we do not apply a migo to invalidate the document in the case of the borrower, so too Rabbi Meir says regarding witnesses that even though they have greater power [than the borrower], they cannot invalidate the document with a migo.

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:4:2.hebrew: מודה בשטר שכתבו א"צ לקיימו - וא"ת: ומ"ט לא מהימן במגו, דאי בעי אמר "מזויף"? וי"ל, דשמא ירא לוה לומר "מזויף" פן יכחישוהו, וליכא מגו. ופירש הקונט' במקום אחר, דטעמא משום דדבר תורה א"צ קיום, דעדים החתומים על השטר נעשה כמי שנחקרה עדותן בב"ד, ורבנן הוא דאצרכוהו קיום כי טעין "מזויף הוא", אבל בשאר טענות, כגון "פרוע הוא", לא הצריכוהו קיום; וכן נראה לר"י. אבל אין לפרש דלא מהימן במגו לומר "פרוע הוא" משום ד"אי פרעיה, שטרא בידיה מאי בעי?", דהא כי טעין נמי "אמנה הוא", מסקינן בסמוך אמילתיה דרב דלא מהימן, והתם לא שייך האי טעמא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:4:2.english: [In the case of one who] admits with regard to a document that he wrote it, [the lender] need not ratify it - And if you ask: Why is he not believed based on a migo [an argument that he could have made a stronger claim], since if he wanted, he could have said, "[It is] forged"? And one can answer: Perhaps a borrower is afraid to say "[It is] forged" lest they contradict him, and [thus] there is no migo. And Rashi explained elsewhere that the reason is that by Torah law it does not need ratification, since witnesses who are signed on a document are treated as if their testimony has been examined in court; and it was the Rabbis who required ratification for it when he claims "It is forged," whereas for other claims, such as "It is paid," they did not require ratification for it — and so it appears to the Ri. However, one should not explain that he is not believed with a migo to say "It is paid" because "if he had paid it, what would the document be doing in his [the lender's] hand?" — for when he claims "It is [a document of] trust" as well, we conclude shortly hereafter regarding Rav's statement that he is not believed, and there that reason does not apply.

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:5:1.hebrew: אי סבירא לך כר"מ כו' - וא"ת: ודלמא משום הכי לא קאמר הלכה כר"מ, משום דאיכא בפ' מי שמת (ב"ב קנד: ושם) דמפיך דר"מ לרבנן? ויש לומר: דהוה מצי למימר דהלכה כרשב"ג, דאית ליה בהדיא בפ"ק דב"מ (דף ז.) דמודה בשטר שכתבו אין צריך לקיימו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:5:1.english: If you hold in accordance with Rabbi Meir, etc. - And if you ask: Perhaps for this reason he did not say [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir, because there is [an opinion] in Chapter Mi Shemeit (Bava Batra 154b, and there) that reverses [the views of] Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis? One can answer: He could have said that the halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who holds explicitly in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (7a) that [when one] admits with regard to a document that he wrote it, [the lender] need not ratify it.

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:5:2.hebrew: אימא הלכה כרבי מאיר - תימה, דאפילו כרבנן נמי מצי סבר, ושאני עדים דאלימי לאורועי שטרא, דהכי אית ליה לרבי יוחנן! ויש לומר דרב נחמן אין נראה לו לחלק. ואם תאמר: ודלמא רב הונא מיירי במודעא ואמנה, דאפילו רב נחמן מודה לקמן? ויש לומר דרב הונא סתם קאמר ולא מפליג:
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:5:2.english: Say: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir - This is astonishing! For [Rav Huna] could even hold like the Rabbis, and witnesses are different because they are strong [enough] to undermine a document, as Rabbi Yoḥanan holds! And it can be answered that it does not seem [correct] to Rav Naḥman to make [this] distinction. And if you will say: Perhaps Rav Huna is speaking of [a claim of] a moda'a [notification of coercion] or [a document of] amana [trust], regarding which even Rav Naḥman agrees below? And it can be answered that Rav Huna stated [his ruling] unconditionally and did not differentiate:

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:9:1.hebrew: לעולם דקאמר לוה וכדרב הונא כו' - ואם תאמר: ואמאי לא קאמר נמי "לעולם דקאמרי עדים וכדרב הונא"? ויש לומר: דלא ניחא ליה לאוקמי דלא כרבנן, דאמרי אלימי עדים לאורועי שטרא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:9:1.english: Actually, [it is] the borrower who is saying [it], and in accordance with Rav Huna, etc. - And if you ask: Why did he not also say, "Actually, [it is] the witnesses who are saying [it], and [it is] in accordance with Rav Huna"? One can answer that he did not want to establish [it] not in accordance with the Rabbis, who say that witnesses have the power to undermine a document.

Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:9:2.hebrew: וכדרב הונא אמר רב - וא"ת, תרתי מילי דרב למה לי? וי"ל דחדא מכלל חבירתה אתמר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 19a:9:2.english: And in accordance with Rav Huna [in the name of] Rav - And if you ask: Why do I need two statements of Rav? One can answer that one was stated by implication from the other.
